recipes.name: Mexican Bean and Rice Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (15.25 ounce) can whole kernel corn, drained
1 (15 ounce) can kidney beans, rinsed and drained
1 (15 ounce) can black beans, rinsed and drained

steps.text: Combine brown rice, corn, kidney beans, black beans, onion, bell pepper, jalapeño peppers, cilantro, lime zest and juice, cumin, and garlic in a large bowl; gently toss until well mixed. Season with salt.
Refrigerate salad for 1 hour, toss again, and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Mexican Bean and Rice Salad
raw_recipe.description: This Mexican-style bean and rice salad recipe comes together quickly and easily using refreshing ingredients bursting with flavor, texture, and color.

review.reviewBody: YUM! I loved the combination of flavors in this! I didn't have jalapeno peppers so I left them out but then it seemed like it needed some spunk so I added a little hot sauce. Also, it says salt to taste, just FYI, I used a little salt when I cooked the rice and then added one tsp. salt to the whole mixture. I diced the green pepper and onion very small to keep them small in proportion to the main ingredients. This is a keeper!

Made this many times. I grill 1-1.5lbs fajita chicken to add along with a 1/2 a small block of Mexican cheese crumbled and a 1/2 a 14oz tub of restaurant style salsa. I also grilled the onions and peppers. I liked it as is and started adding stuff to make it go further. I usually do this as one of my meal preps for my wife and I for lunch for the week, now and then

Great basic recipe! I used 2 cans of black beans and added a can of tomatoes (that included cilantro and jalapeno). I also added two seeded tomatoes, subbed green onions for the onion, and made the dressing separate. For the dressing I used the juice of two limes mixed with garlic olive oil, 3 cloves of minced garlic, cilantro and my favorite Mexican hot sauce along with the cumin. I also added some Marisco's Mexican spice to the salad. This definitely needs to sit for a while to let all the flavors meld together. I'm glad I made it the night before my BBQ (unfortunately I keep taking a spoonful every time I go into the kitchen!)

I think this would have been wonderfully yummy as the recipe was written, but for my own preferences I followed the recommendations of many of the reviewers. I used two limes, green onions and added some tomatoes. I also used only one jalapeno, but since I chopped it so fine I think two would have been good as well. I read the one reviewer complaining about it being bland. You MUST let this sit in the fridge for an hour. The difference is astounding.

This can be served cold or warm. However, I noticed that after I added the rice that it absorbed all of the moisture making this dish somewhat dry.
I did add more lime juice, a chopped up avocado and taco seasoned ground beef which added some flavor.
This recipe is good enough to make again but maybe with a few possible changes... such as instead of mixing in the rice, make spanish rice and do a layered dish with the rice on the bottom and the beans served on top with a handful of tortilla chips on the side with a spoonful of sour cream and spicy salsa.
The possibilities are endless!

Delicious!! I didn’t have green pepper on hand but will definitely use it next time and it will be even better. I also added olive oil and red wine vinegar as other reviewers suggested. Definitely a salad you can make and have for lunch for the whole week. It’s good by itself and also fab with tortilla chips. Also, I didn’t have fresh limes so I used the bottled stuff.....3-4T.

Everytime I make this it goes quickly. I give out the recipe all the time. I don't like brown rice so I use basmati long grain, and I add more lime juice to moisten it a bit. It's great on warm tortillas with grilled chicken or shrimp. Great cool summer lunch too
For fun individual servings I made mini taco salad bowls by using tortillas and baking them on an upside down muffin tin. Once they cooled I spooned in the salad mixture and topped with chunky salsa.

Surprisingly YUM! Used red pepper instead of green, green onion for the white onion. And, added a little olive oil and red wine vinegar. Did not have jalapeños, so added a few drops of smoked chipolte tabasco. Makes a TON. PS: Also, to make it even quicker to put together, used Trader Joe's frozen brown rice - just heat, cool and mix it all together. Will make this again and again!

Love it... with minimal changes. I used 2 cans of Black beans instead of kidney. Used green onions, green chilies (instead of jalapeno). Added chili powder, onion powder. Used 2 limes, dash of balsamic vinegar and EVOO for the dressing. Definitely let it sit overnight. My co-workers loved it :)

A favorite with our family. I've taken it to pot lucks and it's always a hit. Nice vegetarian dish. The cilantro really gives it a fresh taste. Left out the jalapeno peppers and added sweet red pepper for color. With or without the rice, it really makes a nice dip with with scoops.
Feels healthy and feeds plenty and very yummy
Oh I love this! So delicious and fresh!
i left out the 2 jalapeño chile peppers, seeded and diced

Love the recipe! It makes a large portion and it is a perfect side dish for home or to take to a picnic. I did use a pouch of 90 second microwavable cilantro rice which made this super quick to make. If your not a fan of Mexican seasonings an Italian dressing would work well with these ingredients.
Easy and good. BUT!!! Put it atop chips and grate cheese over it. Broil it and yummy!!!!
This salad was the BOMB! Very well balanced, only added 1 jalapeño, and omitted the corn.....will make again.
Very tasty and easy to throw together!

I loved this salad! I used barley instead of brown rice based on personal preference but it's light, filling, and perfect for a quick lunch in the summertime. I've been eating on this all week and, on the suggestion of a couple of other reviews, I put this in a burrito for a change-up. I only used one jalapeno because I'm a wimp but it's still delicious. Big fan of this one!
